title: Premature Fatigue Failure Analysis of Axle in Permanent Magnet Direct-Drive Electric Locomotive (Materials 2025, 18(16), 3747)
content: Research on axle reliability and damage over the years has found that, in addition to wear and tear, about two-thirds of axle damage is caused by fatigue. The fatigue process is particularly sensitive to microstructure, surface conditions, residual stresses, non-metallic inclusions, and stress concentration factors at geometric transitions.

citations.used_for: PRIOR: base rate of fatigue_from_transition_arc_geometry_stress_concentration among premature fatigue fractures of EA1N/UIC 811-1 in-service axles. No published base rate exists for this specific geometric sub-mode. The nearest literature figure is 'about two-thirds of axle damage is caused by fatigue' (root-cited reference [1]), but that is the rate of fatigue overall, not of arc-geometry stress concentration specifically. Reported value 0.67 is a coarse direction-only anchor (fatigue prevalence), NOT a grounded primary base rate for the specific answer. Within fatigue, fretting fatigue at the wheel seat dominates (>90% per enterprise statistics), so arc-geometry stress concentration is plausibly a minority sub-mode — the 0.67 anchor likely overstates the true base rate of this specific mode.->fatigue_from_transition_arc_geometry_stress_concentration
